more.def: A person's son or daughter, no matter how old they are.
examples: My grandmother's children are my mom and my two uncles.
Even as an adult, she is still her parents' child.
The bear led her two children across the stream.

easy.def: The time when you are a child.
examples: In my childhood I lived by the sea.
Grandpa told us about his childhood.
She had a happy childhood.

more.def: The time of life when you are a child.
examples: Grandpa told us stories about his childhood.
She spent her childhood on a farm.
In her childhood, she loved to climb trees.

easy.def: Silly like a baby.
examples: That is childish.
A childish game.
He was childish.

more.def: Acting in a silly way, as a young child would, when you are older.
examples: Throwing a tantrum is childish.
It is childish to stick out your tongue.
His childish behavior surprised us.

easy.def: A hot pepper.
examples: The chili is hot.
I put chili in the soup.
The chili is red.

more.def: A small, hot pepper that is used to flavor food, or a spicy stew made with it.
examples: The chili was too hot for me.
Dad made a pot of chili with beans.
She added a chopped chili to the sauce.

easy.def: A cold feeling.
examples: There is a chill in the air.
I felt a chill.
The chill made me shiver.

more.def: A feeling of being cold, or a cold feeling in the air.
examples: There was a chill in the air that morning.
I felt a chill as I walked outside.
A chill ran down her back at the scary story.

easy.def: To make something cold.
examples: I chill the juice.
Chill the milk.
We chilled the watermelon.

more.def: To make something cool or cold.
examples: We chilled the juice in the fridge.
The cold wind chilled my hands.
Chill the dough for an hour.

easy.def: A little cold.
examples: It is chilly outside.
I wore a coat on the chilly day.
The water is chilly.

more.def: Cool enough to make you feel a little cold.
examples: It was a chilly morning, so we wore our jackets.
The lake water felt chilly on our toes.
A chilly wind blew across the field as the sun went down.

easy.def: To make a soft, ringing sound.
examples: The clock chimes at noon.
The bell chimed softly.
Our doorbell chimes when you push it.

more.def: To make a clear, gentle ringing sound, the way a bell or a clock does.
examples: The old clock in the hall chimes every hour.
The school bell chimed, and everyone lined up quietly.
Soft bells chimed in the breeze outside the window.

easy.def: A soft ringing sound, or a bell that makes it.
examples: We heard the chime of the clock.
A chime hangs by the door.
The chimes sang in the wind.

more.def: A clear, gentle ringing sound, or a set of hanging tubes or bells that make this sound when they move.
examples: The wind made the chimes on the porch ring all afternoon.
We heard the chime of the church bell across the valley.
A happy chime told us that the oven timer was done.

easy.def: A tall pipe that lets smoke out of a house.
examples: Smoke came out of the chimney.
The chimney is made of bricks.
A bird made a nest in the chimney.

more.def: A tall pipe or tube that carries smoke from a fire up and out of a building.
examples: Smoke curled up from the chimney of the small cabin.
Birds sometimes build nests on top of an old chimney.
The sweep cleaned the soot from the chimney before winter.

easy.def: An ape that looks a bit like a person.
examples: The chimp ate a banana.
A chimp climbed the tree.
We saw a chimp at the zoo.

more.def: Short for chimpanzee, a smart ape with long arms that lives in the forests of Africa.
examples: A chimp swung from branch to branch at the zoo.
Chimps use sticks as tools to dig insects out of logs.
The young chimp held tight to its mother's back.

easy.def: The part of your face below your mouth.
examples: I rested my chin on my hand.
She has a dimple on her chin.
Milk dripped down his chin.

more.def: The part of the face below the mouth, at the front of the jaw.
examples: He scratched his chin while he thought.
She has a small dimple in her chin.
Cold water dripped from her chin after she drank from the fountain.

easy.def: A small furry animal with soft gray fur.
examples: A chinchilla is soft.
We have a chinchilla as a pet.
The chinchilla has big ears.

more.def: A small South American animal with very soft, thick gray fur, big ears and a long bushy tail.
examples: The chinchilla has fur so thick and soft that it feels like velvet.
A chinchilla takes a dust bath to keep its fur clean.
Chinchillas live in the mountains of South America.

easy.def: A thin crisp piece of food.
examples: I eat potato chips.
Chips are crunchy.
He ate a corn chip.

more.def: A thin, crisp slice of food that has been fried or baked.
examples: She ate a bag of potato chips.
Corn chips and salsa made a good snack.
The chips were crunchy and salty.

easy.def: A small broken piece.
examples: There is a chip in the cup.
A chip of wood fell.
A paint chip.

more.def: A small piece that has broken off something.
examples: There is a chip in the edge of the cup.
A chip of paint fell from the wall.
The sculptor swept away the stone chips.

easy.def: To break off a small piece.
examples: Do not chip the plate.
The cup chipped.
The paint chipped.

more.def: To break a small piece off something.
examples: Don't chip the plate when you wash it.
The paint chipped off the old fence.
He chipped his tooth on a hard candy.

easy.def: A sweet brown food.
examples: I love chocolate.
Chocolate is sweet.
The chocolate melted.

more.def: A sweet brown food made from cocoa beans.
examples: I ate a piece of chocolate.
The chocolate melted in the sun.
Chocolate cake was served at the party.

easy.def: Made with the sweet brown food.
examples: Chocolate milk.
Chocolate cake.
A chocolate bar.

more.def: Flavored with or made from cocoa.
examples: We drank chocolate milk.
She baked a chocolate cake.
He ate a chocolate bar.

easy.def: When you pick one thing.
examples: It was a hard choice.
You have a choice of two toys.
Make your choice.

more.def: The act of picking one thing from two or more things.
examples: It was a hard choice between the red and blue shirts.
You have a choice of milk or juice.
Her choice was to take the shorter path.

easy.def: A group of singers.
examples: The choir sings.
I am in the choir.
The choir has twenty kids.

more.def: A group of people who sing together, often in a school or church.
examples: The school choir sang a holiday song.
I joined the choir this year.
The choir practiced every Tuesday.

easy.def: To be unable to breathe because something is in your throat.
examples: I choked on a nut.
He choked on the water.
Chew your food so you do not choke.

more.def: To have trouble breathing because something is blocking your throat.
examples: He choked on a piece of bread.
Chew slowly so you do not choke.
The smoke made her cough and choke.

easy.def: To pick one thing.
examples: Choose a book.
I chose the red one.
She chooses a flavor.

more.def: To pick the one you want from two or more.
examples: You may choose a snack from the basket.
She chose the blue bike.
Choose a partner for the game.

easy.def: To cut something into pieces.
examples: Dad will chop the onions.
We chop wood.
She chopped the carrots.

more.def: To cut something into pieces with a quick, hard stroke.
examples: Mom chopped the onions for the soup.
He chopped wood for the campfire.
The chef chopped the herbs into tiny bits.

easy.def: A helicopter.
examples: The chopper flew overhead.
We saw a chopper land.
The chopper carried the doctor.

more.def: A word that people sometimes use for a helicopter.
examples: The chopper flew over the field.
We watched a news chopper circle above the city.
The chopper landed on the roof.

easy.def: Three or more musical notes played at the same time.
examples: She played a chord.
The chord was happy.
I learned a chord.

more.def: A group of three or more musical notes that are played at the same time.
examples: She played a chord on the piano.
I learned a new chord on my guitar.
The song starts with a loud chord.

easy.def: A small job you do at home.
examples: My chore is to feed the dog.
Washing dishes is a chore.
I did my chores.

more.def: A small job that you must do regularly, especially around the house.
examples: Mopping the floor is a tiring chore.
Dad says that washing dishes is a chore.
I did my chores before I played.

easy.def: A group of singers.
examples: The chorus sang.
I am in the school chorus.
The chorus is loud.

more.def: A large group of people who sing together.
examples: The school chorus sang at the concert.
I joined the chorus this year.
The chorus stood in rows on the stage.

easy.def: The part of a song that repeats.
examples: We sing the chorus.
The chorus is catchy.
Everyone joined in the chorus.

more.def: The part of a song that is repeated after each verse.
examples: We all sang the chorus together.
The chorus of the song is easy to remember.
The band played the chorus twice.

easy.def: A holiday on December 25 when many people give gifts.
examples: We decorate a tree at Christmas.
Christmas is in winter.
I sang songs at Christmas.

more.def: A holiday on December 25 that Christians celebrate for the birth of Jesus, when many families also give gifts.
examples: Our family bakes cookies and gives gifts at Christmas.
Lights and wreaths decorate the town before Christmas.
We sang carols at the school concert near Christmas.

easy.def: Round and soft.
examples: The baby has chubby cheeks.
A chubby puppy ran by.
Her hands are chubby.

more.def: Round and soft in shape, with a bit of extra fat.
examples: The baby had chubby cheeks and a big smile.
A chubby puppy waddled across the yard.
He patted the chubby little hamster in the cage.

easy.def: To throw something without much care.
examples: I chucked the ball.
He chucked the paper away.
She chucked a pebble.

more.def: To throw something in a quick, casual way.
examples: He chucked the ball over the fence.
Chuck the old papers in the bin.
She chucked her backpack on the couch.

easy.def: To laugh quietly.
examples: I chuckle at the joke.
Grandpa chuckled.
She chuckled to herself.

more.def: To laugh softly to yourself.
examples: Grandpa chuckled at the funny story.
She chuckled quietly while she read.
I could hear my dad chuckle at the cartoon.

easy.def: To move slowly with a puffing sound.
examples: The little train chugged along.
The old truck chugged up the hill.
The boat chugs by.

more.def: To move along slowly with a steady puffing noise, as an old engine does.
examples: The little steam train chugged up the steep hill.
The old tractor chugged across the field.
The boat chugged slowly down the river.

easy.def: A close friend.
examples: He is my chum.
We are chums.
My chum came over.

more.def: A close friend, especially in an old-fashioned way.
examples: He is my best chum from school.
We have been chums since we were little.
My chum and I rode bikes to the lake.

easy.def: A thick piece.
examples: A chunk of cheese.
I ate a chunk of bread.
A chunk of ice fell.

more.def: A thick, solid piece that has been broken or cut off something.
examples: I ate a chunk of cheese.
A chunk of ice broke off the glacier.
She cut the melon into chunks.

easy.def: A building where Christians pray.
examples: We go to church on Sunday.
The church has a bell.
The church is old.

more.def: A building where Christians gather to pray and worship.
examples: The church bell rings on Sunday.
We went to a wedding at the church.
A tall steeple rises above the church.

easy.def: A slide that things go down.
examples: The mail goes down the chute.
The kids slid down the chute.
The laundry chute is in the hall.

more.def: A narrow, sloping channel that people or things slide down.
examples: The dirty laundry goes down a chute to the basement.
Children whooped as they slid down the water chute.
Grain poured down the chute into the truck.
